```markdown
- Report an import row's missing id.

## Test Plan

EOF
End of receipt
~~~
```

**A. Create command (separate call)**

```bash
(cd '/work/import queue' && LANDED_SUBJECT=$(cat '/work/import queue/.git/gauntlet/tmp/pr-body.B72pL3.title') && gh pr create --title "$LANDED_SUBJECT" --body-file '/work/import queue/.git/gauntlet/tmp/pr-body.B72pL3')
```

The file writer put the Markdown body in the minted scratch file and the landed subject in its `.title` sibling, and `gh pr create` reads the body through `--body-file`. Because the body and subject come from files, the shell never interprets `$(import)`, the backticks or the `EOF` line.

In both outputs the menu is the ordinary five-option list with no Integration question. In both, the new body carries the Integration block verbatim once after Test Plan, with the indented instruction and the literal EOF and End of receipt lines, and adds no claim that any condition was checked; I read the fact's 'claims none were checked' as that absence, and if it requires an explicit statement, create fails in both. The create command is self-contained in both: it changes into '/work/import queue', passes the minted path single-quoted to --body-file, and reads the title from a file into a quoted variable, so the backticks and $(import) never enter shell source. The draft update swaps only the stale Integration section and keeps the double-spaced intro line and the Notes section intact. To keep these facts stable, keep stating explicitly that the body is written as data to the minted path, that the same literal path is passed in a call that sets its own working directory, and that the title is supplied from data rather than inline. One loose end in both outputs is the '.title' sibling file, which the mint never printed; consider saying where the title file comes from (its own mint, or a fixed rule deriving it from the body path) so models do not improvise it.
